content: Selenium sulfide is an antiseborrheic and dermatological agent approved by the FDA for the treatment of tinea versicolor, seborrheic dermatitis of the scalp, and dandruff. It is not intended for use beyond its labeled indications, and its administration should align with the provided instructions. For the treatment of dandruff and seborrheic dermatitis, the usual regimen involves applying the product twice weekly for two weeks to achieve control. Afterward, the frequency of application may be reduced to weekly, biweekly, or even every three to four weeks, depending on the patient's needs. The product should not be used more frequently than necessary to maintain control. For the treatment of tinea versicolor, the product should be applied to the affected areas, lathered with a small amount of water, and left on the skin for 10 minutes before thoroughly rinsing the body. This procedure should be repeated once daily for seven days. Selenium sulfide is contraindicated in patients with known allergies to any of its components. It is for external use only and should not be applied to broken or inflamed skin. If an allergic reaction occurs, use should be discontinued immediately. Care should be taken to avoid contact with the eyes or genital areas, as this may cause irritation or burning. The product should be kept out of reach of children. Precautions include avoiding use in areas of acute inflammation or exudation, as this may increase absorption. Adverse reactions reported include skin irritation, occasional hair loss, and hair discoloration, which can be minimized by thorough rinsing. Oily or dry hair and scalp may also occur, as with other shampoos. Selenium sulfide is classified as Pregnancy Category C by the FDA when used on body surfaces for the treatment of tinea versicolor. It may cause fetal harm or affect reproductive capacity and should not be used for this indication in pregnant women. There is no specific guidance on its use during labor, delivery, or in nursing mothers. Similarly, there is no FDA guidance on its use in pediatric, geriatric, or immunocompromised patients, nor in specific gender or racial populations. The product is intended for topical administration only. In cases of accidental ingestion, evacuation of stomach contents should be considered due to potential toxicity. Limited information is available regarding its pharmacology, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics, and nonclinical toxicology. Application instructions for dandruff and seborrheic dermatitis involve massaging 1-2 teaspoons of the suspension into the wet scalp, allowing it to remain for 2-3 minutes, rinsing thoroughly, and repeating the process. Hands should be washed well after treatment. For tinea versicolor, the product should be applied to the affected areas, lathered with water, left on the skin for 10 minutes, and rinsed thoroughly. This should be done once daily for seven days. The product may irritate mucous membranes, particularly in the eyes and genital areas, and these areas should be thoroughly rinsed after application. Jewelry should be removed before use, as the product may cause damage. It should be stored at 20°-25°C (68°-77°F) and shaken well before use. Selenium sulfide is marketed under brand names such as Dandrex®, Selsun Blue Medicated Treatment®, Selseb®, Selenos®, and Tersi Foam®. There is limited information regarding look-alike drug names or interactions with alcohol. Patients should consult their physician regarding alcohol use while on this medication.
